The associator: where the product bends

[e_i, e_j, e_k] over the 16 basis elements: 1848 of 4096 triples do not associate, each by exactly 2. A picture shows a structure; it is not evidence that the structure means anything beyond its definition.

← Box-kite gallery

About this visual

What you are looking at. The associator of the basis elements, [e_i, e_j, e_k] = (e_i e_j) e_k − e_i (e_j e_k), as a 16 × 16 grid: row i, column j, for one chosen k. A cell is blank when the product is associative there and filled when it is not. The engine calls this the curvature, by analogy: it measures how far the product bends when you regroup it.

How to read it. Slide k from 0 to 15, or switch to 'count over k', which shows for each (i, j) how many k bend it. Click a cell for the exact vector. Dotted lines divide the indices 0…7 (the octonions) from 8…15 (the doubled half). The table underneath counts the non-zero triples in each of the eight blocks.

What it shows. 1848 of the 4096 triples do not associate, and every one of them has norm exactly 2: the grid has two values, 0 and 2, nothing in between. The octonion block (i, j, k all below 8) is NOT flat: 168 of its 512 triples bend, the 7 × 6 × 5 − 42 ordered triples of distinct imaginary units that do not lie on a line. k = 0 never bends (e0 is the identity); k = 8 bends in 168 cells, every other k in 120.

What it does not show. A curvature in any differential-geometric sense: there is no metric or connection here, only a count of failures of one law. And it does not say where the zero-divisors are: the associator is a property of the basis table.

Numbers to check. 1848 non-zero, 2248 zero, 4096 in all; blocks (i, j, k below / above 8): 168, 168, 336, 168, 168, 336, 168, 336; per-k counts 0, 120 × 7, 168, 120 × 7.

running self-check…

Code and data. Everything shown is recomputed in the browser by bk.js (the Cayley–Dickson table by doubling, every product, the group by enumeration) and compared with the numbers the Python engine baked into bk_data.js.

  • ValaQuenta/modules/box_kite/maths.py: the Python engine these pages port and check against (Cayley–Dickson table, assessors, box-kites, associator, the labelled group)
  • ValaQuenta/wiki/box_kite.md: the engine's record page, including 'The group, enumerated'
  • Ainulindale/wiki/84_the_box_kite_debugger.md: the narrative of the box-kite as a debugger
  • ValaQuenta/tests/test_box_kite.py: the tests, including an independent recursive Cayley–Dickson product
